title: Lettered List Retained

illustrates.quote: Numbered or lettered answer lines may be retained, or transcribed as an embedded transcriber’s note. Sample: Answers a-e.

print.notes: PDF page image (p.259) inspected directly: print reads "1. List the Great Lakes" with NO terminal period at all (a heading-style item), while the given braille ends "...,lakes4" (with a period).

braille.notes: Independently re-extracted from source (fixed left margin / line-number field stripped by counting; U+2800→space; trailing spaces removed); confirmed byte-identical to both run A and run B (gold-10-A/gold-10-B) except where differences.md records a correction.

uncertain: Print genuinely has no period after "Lakes" (confirmed against the PDF page image) while the given braille has one — a content-fidelity anomaly of this specific worked example (both A and B independently flagged this same ambiguity), not an Emboss defect. Built here following print exactly (no period), so this is EXPECTED to mismatch on that one character; see differences.md.
resolution: Braille matches both A and B exactly. Print: confirmed against the PDF page image that print has no period; the five lettered choices are blank write-on-lines (".-", no answer text) in both print and braille — Emboss has no dot-5/write-on-line blank-fill mechanism for an exercise item, so these are built as empty text.
